title: Game Math Part 2 · Polar Coordinates 1: Distance, Angles and Aiming

scenes.title: 거리와 각도로 게임의 위치 읽기
lines: How can we describe positions when bullets travel and weapons change direction in a game?
Polar coordinates tell us how far a point is from a center, and in which direction.
In part one, we will observe gameplay, locate points, convert coordinates, and apply the result to rotation and aiming.
Part two will extend these ideas into three dimensions.

scenes.title: 실제 관찰 · 움직이는 캐릭터와 무기
lines: This is a Brotato combat sequence. Pick one weapon beside the character instead of watching the entire battlefield.
The weapon stays around the moving character, while its firing direction changes as targets change.
Separate two questions: where is the character in the world, and in which direction is the weapon relative to that character?
The first is a world position; the second is a position measured from a center.
We will describe the visible motion using coordinates. This does not establish which formulas the game's internal code uses.

scenes.title: 오른쪽을 보고, 돌고, 이동합니다
lines: Choose the origin as our center and the positive x direction as zero degrees. Positive y points upward in this diagram.
Turn counterclockwise first. A clockwise turn can be written as a negative angle.
Then travel the chosen distance to locate a point. We call the distance r and the angle theta.
The point four units right and three units up is also five units away at about 36.87 degrees. The point stays the same; only its address changes.
Fixed distance with changing angle produces a circle. Fixed angle with nonnegative distance produces a ray.

scenes.title: 도와 라디안은 같은 각도의 다른 단위
lines: A common mistake is mixing angle units. One full turn is 360 degrees, or two pi radians.
Radians measure arc length relative to the circle's radius. An arc as long as the radius spans one radian.
Ninety degrees equals pi over two radians. Multiply a degree value by pi and divide by 180 to convert it.
Typical programming math functions take radians. Passing 90 directly to sine does not give the sine of 90 degrees. Check the API and label units in variable names.

scenes.title: 실제 관찰 · 방향과 이동 거리 분리하기
lines: Watch the projectiles traveling away from the character in this encounter. A projectile moves farther from where it was launched.
Travel in a fixed direction can be described by keeping theta constant and increasing r.
To fire in several directions, assign a different angle to each projectile. Launch angle and travel distance are separate controls.
The reference point may be the launch position rather than the character's current position. Moving that reference along with the character is a separate design decision.
Identifying the visible motion helps us decide which quantity stays fixed and which changes.

scenes.title: 좌표는 달라도 같은 점일 수 있습니다
lines: A polar point has more than one address. Adding a full turn to radius three and angle 30 degrees reaches the same point.
Thirty and 390 degrees are different numbers but the same direction. These equivalent representations are called aliases.
A negative radius means traveling backward along the chosen direction. Radius minus three at 30 degrees equals radius three at 210 degrees.
Subtracting a full turn from 210 gives minus 150 degrees, another address for the same point. Negative coordinates are not inherently invalid.
At radius zero, every angle locates the origin. Position at the origin alone cannot tell us which way something faces.

scenes.title: 저장할 때는 대표 표현을 정합니다
lines: Choosing a representative address makes storage and comparisons easier. This is a canonical form.
Here we choose a nonnegative radius and an angle greater than minus 180 degrees and at most positive 180 degrees.
Make a negative radius positive while adding 180 degrees to the angle. Then wrap by full turns into the chosen interval.
Radius minus three at 30 degrees becomes radius three at minus 150 degrees. For radius zero, our storage convention sets the angle to zero.
This reorganizes an address without moving the point. Implement the boundary rule that maps minus 180 to positive 180 as well.

scenes.title: 실제 관찰 · 같은 방향의 다른 숫자
lines: Watch the direction between a weapon and a nearby enemy again. An enemy to the character's left is still easy to represent.
That direction can have a positive or a negative angle. Different stored numbers can point the same way on screen.
Comparing angle numbers directly can miss equivalent directions. Wrap them into a shared range or compare direction vectors.
If an enemy and the character occupy the same position, their displacement is zero. Position alone cannot determine a new aiming direction.
A game can choose to keep the previous aim. Coordinate conventions and gameplay behavior are separate decisions.

scenes.title: 극좌표에서 가로·세로로 바꾸기
lines: Cartesian coordinates may be needed for drawing or collision calculations. Start with a right triangle.
Cosine is horizontal displacement divided by the hypotenuse; sine is vertical displacement divided by the hypotenuse. The hypotenuse is r.
Multiply by r to obtain x equals r cosine theta, and y equals r sine theta.
At radius ten and angle 30 degrees, x is approximately 8.660 and y is five. Convert the angle to radians before calling the functions.
The formulas also work in other quadrants and with negative radii. Think of signed coordinates rather than only unsigned triangle lengths.

scenes.title: 돌아올 때는 atan2를 사용합니다
lines: To convert back, obtain distance using the Pythagorean theorem. In code, hypot handles very large and very small values more robustly.
Using arctangent of y divided by x loses information. Points four, three and minus four, minus three have the same ratio but opposite directions.
Atan2 accepts the two coordinates separately and identifies the quadrant. In this 2D convention, pass y first and x second.
The point zero, five gives an upward angle of 90 degrees. Avoiding explicit division also avoids dividing by zero.
At the origin, direction is geometrically undefined. Set an origin policy independently of the library's returned number, and wrap the result if needed.

scenes.title: 실제 관찰 · 조준 전에 위치를 뺍니다
lines: Choose the character and one enemy in the encounter. The enemy's world coordinate alone is not the angle we need for aiming.
Subtract the firing position from the target position to express the target relative to the shooter.
Apply atan2 to this relative displacement. Moving both points equally to the right leaves the difference unchanged.
Their absolute screen positions may change while their relative direction stays the same. Connect that idea to the weapons facing nearby targets.
Before using a coordinate in a function, identify its origin. If the muzzle differs from the character's center, use the actual firing position.

scenes.title: 회전은 각도를, 이동은 중심을 바꿉니다
lines: If the center is not at the origin, the computed x and y are offsets. Add the center's coordinates to get the world position.
For an orbit, keep radius fixed and continuously increase the angle. Add angular speed times elapsed frame time.
At 90 degrees per second, a frame lasting one second divided by sixty changes the angle by 1.5 degrees. If angles are stored in radians, angular speed must use radians too.
Adding a fixed angle every frame makes rotation speed depend on frame rate. Multiplying by elapsed time prevents that.
Moving the center translates the entire orbit. Screen coordinates may increase downward, so reconcile their axes with our upward-positive mathematical diagram.

scenes.title: 실제 관찰 · 중심과 주변 물체를 함께 보기
lines: Watch how the surrounding weapons follow the character as it moves. Their world positions combine a center and relative offsets.
Imagine freezing the center: only each weapon's position around the character remains. Moving the center then carries that arrangement along.
An orbit feature can similarly manage its center, radius, and angle separately.
We do not need to assume these weapons follow perfect circles. Their placement and attack animations may have additional rules.
Distinguishing the visible action from our mathematical model prevents forcing one formula onto every behavior.

scenes.title: 179도에서 -179도까지는 2도입니다
lines: Smooth aiming needs care at the angle boundary. Suppose the current angle is 179 degrees and the target is minus 179.
Direct subtraction gives minus 358 degrees, but the directions are only two degrees apart on a circle.
Subtract current from target, then wrap the difference to a shortest-turn interval. Here the result is positive two degrees.
At 90 degrees per second over one sixtieth of a second, movement is limited to 1.5 degrees. Advance that far toward the target.
At exactly 180 degrees, both routes are equal, so choose a consistent turn direction. A direct average of two angle numbers can also fail across the boundary.

scenes.title: 실제 관찰 · 가까운 방향으로 바뀌는 공격
lines: Enemies approach from several directions. Follow one weapon and consider how far it would need to turn toward a new direction.
Treating angles only as points on a number line can suggest a long turn when crossing the interval boundary.
We actually compare directions on a circle. Two directions close to the left can still be connected by a small rotation.
This is a method for implementing a smooth turret, not a measurement of this game's weapon rotation speed.
Instant aiming and speed-limited following are gameplay choices. Polar coordinates provide tools for expressing and calculating those choices.
Next, we will use distance and direction to describe displacement as well as position.

scenes.title: 극좌표 벡터는 이동량을 표현합니다
lines: A vector can also be represented by length and direction. A point is a location relative to an origin; a vector describes the same displacement wherever it starts.
Add a vector two units right to one two units upward.
Adding radii and angles separately would give radius four at 90 degrees, which is wrong. The actual displacement is two right and two up.
Convert to Cartesian components and add them to obtain two, two. Converting back gives length two square root two and direction 45 degrees.
Polar form suits rotation and scaling; Cartesian form suits vector addition and many collision calculations. Switch representations to suit the problem.

scenes.title: 실제 관찰 · 이동과 공격을 따로 읽기
lines: Finally, separate the character's movement from a projectile's movement. Simultaneous motion does not require a shared reference point.
Character displacement is the difference between two positions; projectile travel can be measured from its launch point.
When adding displacements, use a common set of axes and add components. Do not blindly add the two radius and angle numbers.
Choose a reference point and axes first, then convert to a representation suited to the calculation.

scenes.title: 직접 풀고, 다음 편으로 연결하기
lines: Finish with two problems. Convert radius minus two at 45 degrees to our canonical form. Pause and try it yourself.
Make the radius positive and add 180 to obtain 225 degrees. Subtract a full turn to get radius two at minus 135 degrees.
Next convert Cartesian point minus three, four. Its radius is five and atan2 gives approximately 126.87 degrees.
Check the quadrant too: the point lies upper-left, not upper-right. A diagram is a useful way to check a numerical answer.
Remember the flow: locate with distance and angle, then convert when needed. Next time we add height and a second angle for 3D positions and cameras.
